title: DEC-240: harden CI (ignore-scripts installs, persist-credentials, exact Quest version, env: for outputs)
description: DEC-240 CI hardening for lore-cli (plan item 13, operator dec-00icl6f = A 2026-10-26T13:43:57Z; token d240-lore-cli; relayed by the leader). CI only: release LCLI-751 stays held; do NOT pin actions by SHA here (Wednesday grooming question; the existing pins are untouched). DEC-240 verbatim from opum-doc 2026-10-25 14:10Z: "1. Install lore and quest in CI with `npm install -g --ignore-scripts <pkg>@<exact>`. Dependency lifecycle scripts never run on a runner. A shrinkwrap shipped inside the lore and quest packages is a later lore-cli/quest-cli option, not part of this decision. 2. Every actions/checkout step sets `persist-credentials: false` unless that job pushes with the token. A job that does push keeps it and says why in a comment. 3. The Quest version is read only from inside the managed Quest block's markers, and must match `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$` exactly. Anything else fails the job by name and never reaches npm as a range. 4. A step output used in a shell step reaches it through `env:`, never interpolated as ${{ }} inside run:. Delivery: this is DEC-182 (1) floor work (CI workflows and installs), so Sonnet or above authors it and Opus reviews it before landing. [...] Proof per repository, both ways: an install with a dependency carrying a deliberately failing postinstall still succeeds; a CLAUDE.md with a partial version fails the read by name." Items 1 and 3 apply only where lore-cli CI installs lore or quest; items 2 and 4 apply to every workflow. Where an item does not apply, the task says so with what was measured. Not landed by the worker: when the PR is green, a detached review worktree is created and the leader spawns the Opus reviewer.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every actions/checkout step in .github/workflows and .github/actions sets persist-credentials: false, except a job that pushes with the token, which keeps it and says why in a comment (DEC-240 item 2); proved by a test or script that fails on a checkout without it and passes on the real tree

No step output or other ${{ }} expression is interpolated inside a run: shell body where the value can come from outside the repository; such values reach the step through env: (DEC-240 item 4); proved by a check that fails on an interpolated one and passes on the real tree

Every CI install of lore or quest from npm uses npm install -g --ignore-scripts <pkg>@<exact> (DEC-240 item 1), or the task records what was measured showing lore-cli CI installs neither from npm; proved both ways, including an install whose dependency carries a deliberately failing postinstall still succeeding

BLOCKED, NOT CHANGED - A (item 1): benchmark/ladybug/package-qualification.ts:339 (npm install --global <root.tgz> <platform.tgz>) and :374 (npm install <root.tgz> <platform.tgz>) install lore on all six release hosts without --ignore-scripts. NOT edited, and no exemption recorded, because adding the flag to :339 defeats what that job qualifies. The step is labelled installing both tarballs into an isolated global npm prefix without script approval, and assertNoInstallScriptApproval (line 1277) fails the job when npm's output matches allow-scripts, unapproved install script, blocked.*install script or @ladybugdb/core, i.e. it measures the user install path's behaviour under npm's script policy. MEASURED 2026-10-26 on npm 12.2.0 with a dependency carrying a postinstall: without the flag npm prints the install-scripts blocked warning (4 matching lines); with --ignore-scripts it prints none (0). So with the flag the assertion could never fire: the check goes vacuous, and the qualification would stop catching a future dependency that needs script approval on a user machine. The lore launcher and platform packages themselves carry no lifecycle scripts (package.json scripts has no install, postinstall or prepare), so the flag would change nothing about what is installed today. :374 is the second install, an isolated Node project; it asserts the absence of @ladybugdb/core on disk, which --ignore-scripts does not affect, but it is the same user install path. Escalated to the leader for a ruling; the widening of installViolations to scan benchmark/ and scripts/ sources waits on that ruling, because adding it before the sites are resolved would either go red or require an exemption.

It is what makes this safe, since npm 12 blocks and reports unapproved scripts rather than running them. (4) A comment at :339 cites DEC-240 (a4), and the scan lists :339 as the single exception. :374 takes --ignore-scripts. If release hosts ever run an npm that executes unapproved scripts by default, the exception lapses and comes back to me." DEC-240 (a5) WINDOWS USER-PATH QUESTION, lore-cli answer: why the qualified install is still the npm-12 user path when Windows takes npm from Node own directory rather than the global prefix. What makes it the user path is the npm that EXECUTES and its install-script policy, not where npm sits on disk. The report records the executed version (platform.npm 12.2.1, read by the exact LORE_QUALIFICATION_NPM executable under the isolated prefix, so the 11.19.0 read could not recur silently), and scriptBlockingProof shows THAT executable blocked and reported an unapproved fixture postinstall with no flag, with empty user and global config and no allow-scripts env. Where npm.cmd finds its CLI (Node directory versus a global-prefix upgrade) is launcher resolution, not install behaviour: the same npm 12.2.1 code and policy run in both. The qualification also isolates prefix, cache and config on every host by design, which a real user does not; that isolation is what makes the policy measurement hermetic, and it applies equally to all six hosts. Honest limit: a Windows user whose npm 12 sits in the default global prefix was not separately qualified; only the npm-12 behaviour of the executed binary was.

ITEM 1, WINDOWS RED: FIXED, test/ladybug-package-qualification.test.ts:1386-1410.
- Quoting is correct for cmd.exe. On win32, Node's spawn with shell:true joins file and args, then runs `cmd.exe /d /s /c "<joined>"`. /s strips the outer quotes, so the shell sees `"C:\Program Files\nodejs\npm.cmd" --version` and the path stays one token.
- Off win32, shell is false and the path goes to exec as a single argv element. No shell is involved, so POSIX quoting does not apply. Leaving it unquoted is correct, because quoting it there would break it.
- The win32 skip cannot be reached on another host. Both the no-throw return at :1392 and the skip reason at :1403-1404 are gated on `process.platform === "win32"` and nothing else, never on what the read produced.
- Off win32 there is no silent path. Any of error, non-zero status, or a non-X.Y.Z stdout makes `readable` false, and that throws at module load, which fails the file. A missing npm falls back to "npm", gets ENOENT, and throws too. A readable non-12 npm skips under a NAMED reason built into the describe title (:1406, :1410). That is the by-design skip for PR CI, not a silent one.
- On win32 a successful read still skips, under the named "POSIX hosts only" reason. So the quoting only improves the printed reason, and the leg's outcome does not depend on it.
- The (a4) condition-2 gate is not weakened. The stat shows benchmark/ladybug/package-qualification.ts untouched. assertNpmMajor at :1479-1488 still requires an exact X.Y.Z with `!== REQUIRED_NPM_MAJOR`. The only production-adjacent change is a test comment, :577, corrected from "12 or later" to "exactly major 12", which now matches the code.

FINDINGS
- LOW, test/ci-hardening.test.ts:207-210. The count is lexical on the identifier `flaglessGlobalInstall(`, so a third caller can dodge it:
  - an import alias (`import { flaglessGlobalInstall as f }` then `f(...)`);
  - a re-export under another name;
  - a reference assigned to a variable, or `.call` / `.apply`;
  - any caller outside benchmark/, scripts/ and docker/, for example src/, which loadSources does not walk.
  Each needs a deliberate rename or a caller in an unusual place. The count over-counts rather than under-counts on odd declaration spacing, so it fails closed there. File as a follow-up per (a6). A fix would also flag any import of flaglessGlobalInstall outside its own file that renames it, or that comes from a file not on a known list.
